principles: Decision first, implementation second: do not build handshake/signing/runner features until PD-1 is explicit.
Authority claims must be mechanical: no CLI mode may imply L2+ trust without server-verifiable evidence and receipts.
Durable truth-source over buried story memory: the final role contract must live in docs/requirements/decisions with story evidence as derivation.
Keep cross-repo ownership clear: CLI, Python authority, and Mac runner follow-ups must name their owning repo and gate dependencies.
drivers: B-0f04 found current CLI evidence submission is below Python production enforce requirements.
Mac/Swift runner already owns signed runner behavior, so duplicating it in CLI is a product decision, not a default implementation detail.
The user wants Claude Code to execute and Codex to verify, so this story needs explicit evidence and review gates rather than informal agreement.

options.name: story-evidence-only decision
pros: Smallest change and fastest to write.
Keeps all B-4bd4 material scoped to the current story.
cons: Future agents may not discover the decision without reading old story evidence.
Does not satisfy product-reviewer durability advisory.
Weakens follow-up story alignment across Koala CLI, Python authority, and Mac runner repos.

options.name: durable truth-source decision plus story derivation
pros: Gives future agents one canonical PD-1 contract in docs/requirements/decisions.
Keeps detailed evidence and tradeoff derivation in B-4bd4 story evidence.
Directly addresses INIT reviewer advisories and makes Milestone 2-6 routing explicit.
cons: Touches a project decision doc, so docs reviewer must confirm this is appropriate for an audit/decision story.
Requires careful wording to avoid pretending implementation already exists.

options.name: skip decision and start enforce-mode implementation
pros: Would immediately produce code toward FU-1/FU-2/FU-3.
Could be attractive if the team already knew CLI must be first-class.
cons: Contradicts B-0f04 recommendation to resolve PD-1 first.
Risks building actor/signature/runner behavior that the product may not want in CLI.
Would blur PM/verifier and implementer roles.

chosen: durable truth-source decision plus story derivation
rationale: Choose the durable truth-source decision approach. B-4bd4 must produce a discoverable PD-1 contract before implementation starts, while retaining story-scoped evidence for auditability.

preMortem.scenario: The decision artifact says CLI is enforce-mode but later implementation discovers CLI cannot safely own runner identity.
preMortem.trigger: Decision ignores Mac runner responsibilities and Python actor-key requirements.
preMortem.consequence: FU-1/FU-2/FU-3 waste effort and may weaken authority boundaries.
preMortem.mitigation: Require the decision to compare thin CLI versus enforce-mode CLI against B-0f04 evidence and explicitly state L2+ trust consequences.

preMortem.scenario: The decision lives only in B-4bd4 evidence and future agents miss it.
preMortem.trigger: Follow-up stories search docs/requirements/decisions but do not inspect old story evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Agents reopen PD-1 or implement conflicting behavior.
preMortem.mitigation: Create docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md as the durable contract and link back to B-4bd4 evidence.

preMortem.scenario: The story overclaims that PD-1 solves flow/fact forgery by itself.
preMortem.trigger: Decision prose treats a role boundary as equivalent to implemented receipt verification or signed evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Gate policy may trust local JSON or natural-language pass claims too early.
preMortem.mitigation: Decision must label Milestones 2-6 as follow-up implementation and state which guarantees remain unavailable until those stories land.

preMortem.scenario: Follow-up routing is too vague for multi-repo execution.
preMortem.trigger: Routing table names features but not owning repo, dependency, or whether it is required/deferred/docs-only.
preMortem.consequence: Claude agents start work in the wrong repo or duplicate existing backlog.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-003 must produce a table mapping Milestone 2-6 to owning repo, status after PD-1, prerequisites, and validation expectation.
